question: How does repeated freshness recomputation at terminal completion scale with the number of enrolled local CPU jobs, and can it be reduced without weakening freshness checks at commit or export?

workload.candidate: One unchanged deterministic local Git candidate and one locked fixture task are enrolled under distinct job IDs. The completion loop is serial and uses an operational-error terminal record so this measurement isolates coordinator freshness validation, not grader throughput or candidate acceptance.
workload.timed_region: Sequential claim and terminal completion transitions after enrollment; candidate/task construction and database enrollment are outside the timer.
workload.primary_metric: Count of durable.inputs calls made while committing all terminal completion transitions for each job count.
secondary_metrics: input checks during full export refresh

comparison.intervention: At completion, recompute freshness for the claimed job only. Retain per-job freshness checks before grading, the startup refresh, and full-bundle freshness refresh at export.

acceptance: All claims are issued and each internal_error terminal transition is committed exactly once; observed completion input-check counts match the frozen expectations; full export recomputes every enrolled job's freshness and every exported bundle passes offline audit. Both summaries bind the exact committed durable.py and measurement-script hashes. Timing is reported descriptively and is not a portable speedup claim.
abort: Abort and preserve outputs on any unexpected claim, commit, count, source-hash or audit result. Do not alter workload, primary metric or protocol after observing measurements.
claim_limit: Same-host synthetic coordinator-work measurement over repeated identical, unchanged candidate inputs. It does not measure heterogeneous grading throughput, candidate acceptance, agent/model capability, multi-host operation, hostile writers, or external usefulness. Operation counts establish scaling of this validation path; timing is machine-local.
